units.title: Being Responsible
units.intro: Grammar: modal verbs for obligation (must, have to, should) and for inference (must be, can’t be, must have).

cards.title: Modals for obligation and advice
rule: **must / have to** = strong obligation: *You **must** wear a helmet.* **mustn’t** = it is not allowed. **don’t have to** = it is not necessary.
**should / ought to** = advice or duty: *We **should** look after our parents.* All modals are followed by the **base verb** (no to after must/should/can).

examples.text: You don’t have to pay; it’s free.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Which of the following sentences exhibits the correct English word order ($$\text{S-V-O}$$)?

steps.text: English requires a strict Subject-Verb-Object ($$\text{S-V-O}$$) pattern.
The subject is 'The security guard', the verb is 'locked', and the direct object is 'the main gate'.
Option A and Option C place the verb ('locked') at the end of the clause, which is an $$\text{S-O-V}$$ pattern typical of Tigrinya grammar (ሓላው ሰላም ማዕጾ ዓጸዎ) and represents a common L1 transfer error.

cards.answer: The security guard locked the main gate at midnight.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Identify the sentence that contains a copula verb error caused by L1 interference.

steps.text: Every English sentence expressing a state of being requires an explicit copula verb ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were') between the subject and the predicate nominative.
In Option C, the copula verb 'is' is completely missing.

In Tigrinya, the copula can sometimes be omitted or structurally merged, leading students to translate "ሓወይ ኣብቲ ዓዲ ትጉህ ሓረስታይ [እዩ]" directly as "My brother a hardworking farmer..." without including the essential English copula 'is'.

cards.answer: My brother a hardworking farmer in the village.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Choose the sentence that correctly manages sentence boundaries without creating a comma splice.

options.A: The rain was heavy, we decided to stay indoors.
options.B: The rain was heavy we decided to stay indoors.
options.C: The rain was heavy; therefore, we decided to stay indoors.
options.D: Because the rain was heavy, so we decided to stay indoors.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
A comma splice occurs when two independent clauses are joined with only a comma. Option A is a comma splice. Option B is a run-on sentence. Option C uses a semicolon and a conjunctive adverb ('therefore'), which is structurally perfect.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Option D is a double-conjunction error ('Because... so...'). Tigrinya speakers often use both because they translate morphological markers like "ስለዝ-... ስለዚ..." directly into English. Option C correctly separates the clauses.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ክልተ ናጻ ዝኾኑ ምሉእ ሓሳባት (independent clauses) ብኮማ ጥራይ ከተኣሳሰሩ ኣይኽእሉን እዮም (እዚ Comma Splice ይበሃል)። ኣብ Option C ዝተጠቐስናሉ ሰሚኮለን (;) ንሰንሰለት ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብግቡእ ይዓጽዎ። Option D ድማ 'Because' ን 'so' ን ብሓባር ብምጥቃም ዝተገብረ ልሙድ ናይ ትርጉም ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Complete the sentence with the correct word order: 'The school principal ________.'

options.A: yesterday welcomed the new students warmly
options.B: warmly welcomed the new students yesterday
options.C: welcomed yesterday warmly the new students
options.D: the new students welcomed warmly yesterday

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
English adverbs of manner ('warmly') usually precede the main verb or follow the object. Adverbs of time ('yesterday') belong at the end of the sentence. The correct structure is: Subject ('The school principal') + Adverb of Manner ('warmly') + Verb ('welcomed') + Object ('the new students') + Adverb of Time ('yesterday').

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Option D shows $$\text{S-O-V}$$ word order. Option A places the time adverb ('yesterday') between the subject and the verb, which is acceptable in Tigrinya but highly irregular and awkward in English unless formatted as a fronted adverbial.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ናይ ግዜ ተወሳኺ ሓበሬታ (Adverb of Time - 'yesterday') ወትሩ ኣብ መወዳእታ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ክስራዕ ከሎ፡ ናይ ኣገባብ ተወሳኺ ሓበሬታ (Adverb of Manner - 'warmly') ድማ ቅድሚ እቲ ዋና ግሲ ይመጽእ። Option B ነዚ ናይ $$S-V-O$$ ስርዓት ብትኽክል ዝሓለወ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "You ____ come with us if you don't want to." Choose the best modal.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "if you don't want to" shows a free choice.

**Step 2:** No obligation is expressed by don't have to.

**Step 3:** "mustn't" would forbid coming, which does not fit.

**Tip:** Obligation: must / have to; no obligation: don't have to; prohibition: mustn't; advice: should / ought to. Inference: must (sure yes), can't (sure no), might/may/could (possible).

cards.title: Modals for inference
rule: When we are almost sure something is true: **must be**: *He has worked all day. He **must be** tired.* Almost sure it is not true: **can’t be**: *That **can’t be** Lula; she is in Keren.*
About the past: **must have + past participle**: *The ground is wet. It **must have rained**.* **can’t have + pp**: *She **can’t have seen** us.*

examples.text: The lights are off. They must be asleep.

cards.pattern: must be / can’t be  ·  must have + past participle

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "She must has left."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** When we are almost sure something is true: **must be**: *He has worked all day. He **must be** tired.* Almost sure it is not true: **can’t be**: *That **can’t be** Lula; she is in Keren.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "She must has left." breaks this rule.
**Check:** About the past: **must have + past participle**: *The ground is wet. It **must have rained**.* **can’t have + pp**: *She **can’t have seen** us.*

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **Must** = 99% sure or a rule; **can’t** = 99% sure it’s not; add **have + pp** to look back.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Must/have to show obligation, should gives advice, mustn’t forbids, don’t have to means not necessary. For inference use must be / can’t be (present) and must have / can’t have + past participle (past).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Choose the alternative that best represents the italicized sentence: *It isn't necessary to translate every word.*

options.A: You don't have to translate every word.
options.B: You must not translate any word.
options.C: You have to translate almost all of the words.
options.D: You must translate all of the words.
options.E: It isn't necessary to translate any word.

cards.why:
The phrase 'It isn't necessary' expresses a **lack of obligation**. In English, the modal phrase **'don't have to'** is used to show that something is not required or necessary. 

*   **'Must not'** (Option B) means prohibition (you are forbidden).
*   **'Have to'** (Option C/D) means obligation (you are required).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Her eyes are red and she is holding a tissue. She ____ have been crying.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The evidence (red eyes, tissue) makes the speaker nearly sure.

**Step 2:** must have + past participle = strong inference about the past.

**Step 3:** "can't have" would mean she surely was not crying.

**Tip:** Obligation: must / have to; no obligation: don't have to; prohibition: mustn't; advice: should / ought to. Inference: must (sure yes), can't (sure no), might/may/could (possible).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Somebody is knocking. It ____ be the postman; he usually comes at this time."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The speaker thinks it is possible because of the usual time.

**Step 2:** could/might/may express possibility.

**Step 3:** "can't" means impossible; "mustn't" is prohibition.

**Tip:** Obligation: must / have to; no obligation: don't have to; prohibition: mustn't; advice: should / ought to. Inference: must (sure yes), can't (sure no), might/may/could (possible).

glossary.meaning: A helping verb such as must, should, can that adds meaning.

tips.text: **Must** = 99% sure or a rule; **can’t** = 99% sure it’s not; add **have + pp** to look back.
